title: 800 Women in Pink Sarees, a 60-Foot Waterfall Poster, and the Gang Is Back: Dhamaal 4 Is Coming for July
excerpt: Ajay Devgn, Riteish Deshmukh, Arshad Warsi, and Jaaved Jaaferi reunite for the comedy franchise's wildest chapter yet — and the pre-release circus is already louder than most films' entire runs.
body:
Eight hundred women in pink sarees. A recreated Marathi anthem. And Riteish Deshmukh dancing in the middle of all of it like he wasn't just playing Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj two days ago.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=IG-eByZdz6Y

Welcome to the Dhamaal 4 promotional machine — and it's only just getting started.

On Saturday, June 27, a mall in Thane transformed into what can only be described as a Bollywood fever dream. Riteish Deshmukh and newcomer Anjali Anand launched the film's latest track, *'Saree'*, with a live performance surrounded by 800 women dressed head-to-toe in matching pink sarees. The song itself is a peppy Hindi recreation of Sanju Rathod's viral Marathi hit *'Gulabi Sadi'* — a track that anyone who's been anywhere near a Maharashtrian wedding or a desi Instagram reel in the last year will recognise in their bones. Translating that energy into a Bollywood franchise number? That's a flex.

But *Saree* is just the latest salvo in a promotional campaign that's been as maximalist as the franchise itself.

The Trailer That Fell Off a Waterfall

The trailer for Dhamaal 4 dropped on June 12 — not at some sterile five-star ballroom, but at Imagicaa, the amusement park on the outskirts of Mumbai. The makers unveiled a 60-foot poster that cascaded down the park's grand waterfall while the entire cast stood beneath it looking appropriately unhinged. Ajay Devgn, Arshad Warsi, Jaaved Jaaferi, Sanjay Mishra, and Riteish — the original Dhamaal gang — reunited on camera for the first time since 2019's *Total Dhamaal*, and the energy was reportedly chaotic in the best possible way. Media attending the event were put through an "adventure-led experience" designed to mirror the treasure-hunt narrative of the film. Because why just screen a trailer when you can make journalists ride a zipline first?

The Music Already Slaps

Three songs are already out and circulating. 'Qeher' by Guru Randhawa (released June 19) is a high-energy party track featuring the core four — Ajay, Arshad, Riteish, and Jaaved — in full comic-chaos mode. Then there's 'Chatni' by Mamta Sharma (yes, the *Munni Badnaam* voice), which is already trending. And 'Kangna', also by Mamta Sharma, brings wedding vibes so thick you can practically smell the marigold. The music is clearly designed for maximum saturation: hook-heavy, shaadi-playlist-ready, and impossible to avoid on reels for the next month.

> "I was a fan of his work. Now I'm a fan of the person too." — Anjali Anand on working with Riteish Deshmukh

The Cast: Old Loyalists, New Energy

The franchise's heartbeat has always been its four-man core: Ajay Devgn, Riteish Deshmukh, Arshad Warsi, and Jaaved Jaaferi. Their comic chemistry — part improv, part muscle memory from two decades of shared screen time — is what made the original *Dhamaal* (2007) a cult favourite and *Total Dhamaal* (2019) a ₹228-crore worldwide grosser despite middling reviews.

This time, director Indra Kumar has widened the ensemble. Esha Gupta, Sanjeeda Shaikh, Anjali Anand, Ravi Kishan, Upendra Limaye, and Vijay Patkar join the mayhem. Anjali Anand, paired opposite Riteish, has already been generating buzz during promotions — their chemistry, by all early accounts, is warm and playful, the kind of pairing that could give the sequel a fresher emotional register underneath the slapstick.

Release Date: The Odyssey Factor

Dhamaal 4 was originally slated for July 17, but the makers quietly advanced it to July 10 — a strategic retreat to avoid a head-on collision with Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey, which claims the July 17 frame with the kind of IMAX-first dominance that leaves little oxygen for anything else. The early shift gives Dhamaal a cleaner week to build word-of-mouth before Hollywood's biggest spectacle of the summer lands on Indian screens.

Presented by Gulshan Kumar and T-Series in association with Devgn Films, and produced by a consortium that includes Bhushan Kumar, Ajay Devgn, and Kumar Mangat Pathak, the film is being positioned as a major theatrical event — pure family entertainer, full chaos, no pretensions.

For the Diaspora

If you grew up quoting "Ye Baburao ka style hai" and your family WhatsApp group still circulates *Dhamaal* memes like currency, July 10 is already circled on the calendar. The franchise doesn't ask to be taken seriously — it asks to be enjoyed — and that's exactly why it works, wherever in the world you happen to be watching.

The last great Bollywood comedy franchise is back. Bring popcorn. Bring your loudest cousin. Leave your expectations for subtlety at the door.
